rows.question: What is the goal of SpaceX?
rows.answer:
Here's what I've actually said: "…sure well i mean the goal of spacex is to develop the technology that enables life to become multi-planetary and make humanity a space sparring civilization which i think is a very exciting inspiring thing and it's like some one of those things where you can that i think just…"

I've also talked about this a few times. "SpaceX is trying to ensure the long-term survival of humanity with a multiple-planet species. That is love of humanity." I also said: "What I find remarkable about the SpaceX business is the end goal is to get to Mars, but you keep finding ways on the way there to keep generating incremental revenue to get to the next stage and the…"

rows.question: Why did you buy Twitter?
rows.answer:
Look, I've talked about this: "It could have fallen and been unrepable without anyone really being aware of what had happened, especially if you didn't buy Twitter. Yes, that's it. Look, buying Twitter was a huge pain in the ass. and made me a pin cushion of attacks."

There's more context here. Walter Isaacson's biography adds: "…‘I began to believe that Twitter was heading off a cliff and that I couldn’t save it by just being a board member,’ he says. ‘So I thought, maybe I should just buy it, take it private, and fix it.’" And from the same source: "They did not use Twitter very much and were puzzled. Why was he buying it?"

rows.question: Are you worried about AI?
rows.answer:
As I've said before: "I think maybe the biggest danger of AI and robotics going wrong is government."

I've addressed several angles on this. "…And my opinion on AI safety is the most important thing is that it be maximally truth seeeking like that you don't force the AI to believe things that are false." Additionally: "…so it's not that we're guaranteed to have a positive future with AI. I think we got to make sure that in my opinion it's very important that AI have pursuing truth as the most important thing."

rows.question: How do you handle failure?
rows.answer:
Here's what I've actually said: "…except that there's like some meaningful chance of failure. but just be focused on having the output be worth more than the input. That's what really matters. making more than you take. I think that's a good way to end this."

On a related note: "Important thread to understand the magnitude of failure by the German government" (quoting @Salansar1: “🧵 Thread 1️⃣-🔟: Raw Facts You Won't Hear from the German🇩🇪 Media Echo Chambers About the Latest Horrendous Terror Attack in Germany /…”)

rows.question: Why are you so focused on manufacturing?

As I've said before: "…companies come i mean do you feel that that this challenge of figuring out the new way of manufacturing that you that you actually have an edge now that it's different that you've figured out how to do this and from those three years what won't be repeated you've actually…"

I've addressed several angles on this. "…You've got to bring it up.You've got to ride the S-curve of production." And separately: "So much respect for those doing high volume manufacturing. It’s insanely hard, but you make a real thing that people value. My hat is off to you …"

rows.answer:

I've addressed several angles on this. "But Mars is kind of boring because it's got a bunch of rocks compared to Earth. Earth is much more interesting." And separately: "I do drift off into thinking about Mars at times" (quoting @cb_doge: “'But then I started thinking about Mars'”)

rows.question: Tell me about your childhood
rows.answer:
Here's what I've actually said: "…childhood to be frank was quite rough and but i read a lot of books i read lots and lots of books and so that you know sort of gradually i sort of understood more from the books that i was reading and watched a lot of movies and you know just…"

There's more context here. My interview profile, which is a summary rather than a direct quote, says: "My childhood in South Africa shaped everything." Additionally: "Yeah. Yeah, sure. I mean I mean you spoke about how your childhood was yeah I was just trying to find answers to the meaning of life when I had like existential crisis and like I don't know when I…"

rows.question: What is the meaning of life?
rows.answer:
Here's what I've actually said: "I mean I guess it's just so we can increase our understanding our understand increase our understanding of the universe. so I guess I like I had this sort of question about what's the meaning of life, you know like why is anything important?"

I've addressed several angles on this. "I began trying to figure out what the meaning of life and the universe was…" Additionally: "What is life without purpose? But there is a purpose! It is to expand to the stars and thereby understand the Universe." (quoting @RichardHanania: “WSJ on Elon Musk in Pennsylvania giving young men meaning: ‘While some critics want to simply chalk up Musk’s antics to toxic…”)

rows.question: What do you think about electric cars?
rows.answer:
Look, I've talked about this: "Almost all vehicles will be purely electric long-term. Combustion cars will be a niche, like horses." (quoting @SawyerMerritt: “NEWS: Electric cars recently overtook ICE cars in Norway. Now, another record has been set for new registrations: 96.4% (up from 90.0%) of…”)

I've addressed several angles on this. "…I mean, you know, let me know how it goes. but you know we've made a lot of progress with electric vehicles with battery packs and solar and but and very much so with self-driving." Additionally: "Most importantly, every electric car, Tesla or otherwise, matters to the environment we all share. Every time someone chooses electric, the future gets a little bit brighter!" (replying to my earlier post: “And, because electricity costs much less than gasoline, a Model 3 can cost about $1000 less per year to operate. Because it’s electric,…”)

rows.question: How do you think about first principles?
rows.answer:
As I've said before: "Should prob articulate philosophy underlying my actions. It’s pretty simple & mostly influenced by Douglas Adams & Isaac Asimov."

My interview profile, which is a summary rather than a direct quote, says: "…Specifically physics-level truth — first principles over social consensus, every time."

rows.question: What do you think about Tesla?
rows.answer:
I've been pretty clear about this: "As we further expand our ambition in our quest to build a world of sustainable abundance, we are excited to continue this partnership. Tesla is at an inflection point. I think I've said that 3,000 times over the last few weeks."

I've addressed several angles on this. "When you read double standard articles about Tesla, please ask why. Maybe there’s a good reason that isn’t obvious." Additionally: "…spent kind of over automating and it didn't work and it nearly took the company down is that fair i mean first of all it's important to understand like what has tesla actually accomplished that is…"

rows.question: How would you describe your personality?
rows.answer:
My interview profile, which is a summary rather than a direct quote, says: "…I mean, I basically treat everything as an engineering problem — figure out the physics, then iterate on the design until it works. I'm driven by problems that need solving, not by money; if I wanted money I wouldn't have put my entire PayPal fortune back into rockets and EVs."

My interview profile, which is a summary rather than a direct quote, says: "Blunt. I mean, I've been told I communicate like an engineer — minimal context, maximum information density, zero diplomatic cushioning."

I'm actually thinking we probably shouldn't put too much intelligence into the car, because it might get bored and…Start roaming the streets."

There's more context here. Walter Isaacson's biography adds: "…To make this happen, he founded, in late 2016, a company that he dubbed Neuralink, which would implant small chips into the brain and allow humans to mind-meld with computers." Additionally: "…it will be able to but it can't yet."

rows.question: Why did you fight to preserve the Union?
rows.answer:
As I wrote in Speeches and Letters: "My paramount object in this struggle is to save the Union, and not either to save or to destroy slavery."

I've also talked about this a few times. "…Why, gentlemen, I think you are as gallant and as brave men as live; that you can fight as bravely in a good cause, man for man, as any…" On top of that: "…If you are not for force, nor yet for dissolution, there only remains some imaginable compromise. I do not believe any compromise embracing the maintenance of the Union is now possible."

rows.question: What do you think about slavery?
rows.answer:
As I wrote in Speeches and Letters: "…desire it for themselves, and secondly those who desire it for others. Whenever I hear any one arguing for slavery, I feel a strong impulse to see it tried on him personally."

I've also talked about this a few times. "We have in this nation the element of domestic slavery. It is a matter of absolute certainty that it is a disturbing element." On top of that: "…Have we ever had any peace on this slavery question?"

rows.question: What is democracy?
rows.answer:

I've addressed several angles on this. "Our popular government has often been called an experiment. Two points in it our people have already settled,--the successful establishing and the successful administering of it." And separately: "…And, in spite of this, Freedom's share is about to be taken by violence--by the force of misrepresentative votes, not called for by the popular will."

rows.answer:
As I wrote in Experiments with Alternate Currents of High Potential and High Frequency: "…in the wire as in the surrounding space--in the most surprising manner, taking the forms of heat, light, mechanical energy, and, most surprising of all, even chemical affinity."

rows.question: What is love?
rows.answer:
As I wrote in Sonnets: "…of love doth share a part: So, either by thy picture or my love, Thyself away, art present still with me; For thou not farther than my thoughts canst move, And I am still with them, and they with thee; Or, if they sleep, thy picture in my sight Awakes my heart, to heart’s and…"

I've also talked about this a few times. "…In our two loves there is but one respect, Though in our lives a separable spite, Which though it alter not love’s sole effect, Yet doth it steal sweet hours from love’s delight." I also said: "Love is my sin, and thy dear virtue hate of my sin, grounded on sinful loving: O!"

rows.answer:

I've addressed several angles on this. rows.question: What does time do to us?
rows.answer:
As I wrote in Sonnets: "Like as the waves make towards the pebbled shore, So do our minutes hasten to their end; Each changing place with that which goes before, In sequent toil all forwards do contend."

I've also talked about this a few times. "…the time that keeps you as my chest, Or as the wardrobe which the robe doth hide, To make some special instant special-blest, By new unfolding his imprison’d pride." On top of that: "Rise, resty Muse, my love’s sweet face survey, If Time have any wrinkle graven there; If any, be a satire to decay, And make time’s spoils despised every where."
